newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia tense as troops move, PM seeks Pol Pot.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia tense as troops move, PM seeks Pol Pot.

text.p: Cambodia's capital was tense on Thursday after a clash between troops loyal to the country's rival leaders.

First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh repeated calls for Khmer Rouge rebels to hand over their ailing former leader Pol Pot in what officials and military analysts described as a "strained" security situation.
"We think the situation is fragile in Phnom Penh, it's not good," Serey Kosal, Ranariddh's top security adviser, told Reuters.
"If the CPP continues to move troops against us we think there's going to be a problem, civil war," he said, referring to Second Prime Minister Hun Sen's Cambodian People's Party.
The two prime ministers, who head a deadlocked coalition government, have been in a bitter power struggle for more than a year.
The unravelling of the Khmer Rouge and capture of the hated Pol Pot last month has inflamed their dispute, exposing deep divisions over how to deal with the rebels.
General Mol Reup, a senior military adviser to Hun Sen, said Ranariddh's men were using "illegal forces" to create instability.
"The Second Prime Minister has got the right to order government troops to maintain security and prevent turmoil," the general told Reuters.
The general was apparently referring to reports that Ranariddh's military commanders were bringing Khmer Rouge defectors into the city to beef up royalist troop strength.
Hun Sen warned this week that he would use force if he found Ranariddh's military men bringing Khmer Rouge defectors into the capital. Ranariddh denied his men were doing so.
Military and political analysts said the wrangle could spark confrontation.
"Categorically tense," said one military attache when asked what he thought of the political mood.
"I'd be surprised if we got through the next few days without something happening," said a political analyst.

Troops loyal to the rival premiers clashed north of Phnom Penh on Wednesday after days of movements around the capital. Military officials said the clash, which left at least one soldier wounded, followed an argument over an unofficial military road block on a main road north of the city.
Security sources said both sides have been setting up checkpoints in recent days to monitor or block their rivals' troop movements.
Ranariddh said on Thursday he had sent his top negotiator to meet the Khmer Rouge guerrillas holding their former leader Pol Pot and to urge them to hand him over to the government quickly.
Ranariddh said his negotiator travelled to the guerrillas' base at Anlong Veng in northern Cambodia on Thursday to seek a speedy end to the Pol Pot issue.
He hinted that the powerful Hun Sen might try to use the Khmer Rouge problem as an excuse to attack him and his royalist FUNCINPEC party.
"A group wants to use the Anlong Veng problem for a military attack on FUNCINCPEC," the prince said without naming Hun Sen.
Hun Sen was out of the country on Thursday, an aide said. He declined to release details of the second prime minister's trip.

Ranariddh says his aim is to end the war with the Khmer Rouge and bring peace to the country but he has also said he would be willing to bring Khieu Samphan, and his more moderate Khmer Rouge followers, into his political alliance.
Hun Sen declared any talks with the guerrillas illegal.
The two premiers are trying to bolster their positions in the run-up to a general election in May next year.
